$doc: WHAT A CITY BELIEVES - the faith half of a city's taste (docs/PRICE_FACTORS.md §3.1, slice P1).
note: The owner, 2026-10-18: 'is there a way for the prices move on many different factors? like relationship with other countries, religion, merchants'. A port's faith comes from the culture it already carries (ports.culture, scripts/lib/world-derive.mjs), with the named exceptions below. A culture or port not listed has no faith row: its goods carry no faith taste. Each line is defended, because a seeded faith can invent a belief but it cannot mean one.

cultures.why: Catholic Iberia, Italy, France and their colonies
England and its colonies, Protestant after 1534
the Hanse and the Low Countries, Lutheran and Reformed
the Ottoman, Persian, Arab and Maghrebi lands
the Swahili coast's towns were Muslim from the twelfth century
Malacca, Aceh, Banten, Demak and Ternate were sultanates by 1550
the coasts of India, Hindu in their people under Hindu and Muslim rulers alike
Ming China's temples, beside Confucian rites
Joseon kept its Buddhist temples under a Confucian court

ports.why: Hanoi, Dai Viet's Buddhist and Confucian capital
Hoi An, a Vietnamese and Chinese port of temples and clan halls
Cebu, where Legazpi founded the first Spanish town in 1565
